issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) require Farm.animals to be a List<Animal> (and instruct to implement it using an ArrayList), but the solution implementation uses a Set<Animal> (HashSet). This mismatch between the specified collection type and the solution's collection type is structural: it affects the expected API (getter/setter types) and the iteration order semantics students might rely on when implementing or testing singFarmSong().
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification by changing Farm.animals to a List<Animal> and initializing it as an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. Update the getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>, import java.util.List and java.util.ArrayList, and keep iteration logic compatible (for-each over the List). Alternatively, if Sets are intentional, update the problem statement and UML to specify a Set and remove the explicit ArrayList requirement so all artifacts agree.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly specifies that Farm should aggregate animals using a List and that the ArrayList should be initialized in the no-argument constructor, but the solution implementation declares and uses a Set (HashSet) for the animals collection. This mismatch between 'List/ArrayList' (problem/template expectation) and 'Set/HashSet' (solution) creates a mapping confusion for students: they are instructed to use a List/ArrayList but the reference solution uses a different collection type name.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the collection type across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to use List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() (change imports, field type, getter/setter types, and constructor), matching the problem statement and template instructions; or (B) if Set semantics are intended, update the problem statement and template instructions to explicitly require a Set/HashSet so students are not instructed to use a List/ArrayList.
